report.outcome:
**SECURED — w20 / 600.000 s / 200 gold / 927 kills / 91 calls**, `defaultedSecure: 1`, `defaultedPicks: 0`.

- **2 sim runs, 1 scored attempt.** Run 1 = the ten-second idle probe. Run 2 = `ctrl-v1`, which secured on its first ride.
- **Tape put forward: `attempt-1-tape.json`** — declared in `gauntlet-outcome.json`'s `tape` field. It is a **byte-identical copy** of `tune-1-tape.json` (247,848 B, `Buffer.compare` = 0): **one ride under two filenames.** The stop rule ends the heat at the first SECURED outcome, so the securing tune is promoted by name rather than re-ridden.
- **Envelope, measured on the first reel that existed:** `durationTicks` 18,000 · last accepted order at tick **17,578** · 91 entries of 3,601 · 247,848 B. `twist.clockTicks` is 18,000 and a wave-20 secure lands at t = 600 = tick 18,000, so the F-HEAT11-1 terminal-tick hazard is **live on this contract**; the reel sits 422 ticks clear of it.
- **Receipt, control-tested first:** the zero-order idle probe replayed to its own header (`fnv1a32:a45ba9ac`) exactly — instrument verified — and only then did the promoted reel reproduce `fnv1a32:737ded35` with `securedSnapshot {waves: 20, gold: 200, timeAlive: 600}`, which is exactly what the door's `score_mismatch` rule compares against the declared gold. (That is the **tape header's** hash; the stdout outcome line's `fnv1a32:02ba8fff` is a different number by design.)
- Gold is the only free ranking axis here (waves and `timeAlive` are pinned by the wave-20 secure) and **200 is the live cap**, reached at t = 516 and held to the bank.
report.whatTheMapAsked: It asked me about **anchoring, once, before the first enemy spawned, and the answer was a disc** — so E9's signature mechanic is genuinely live, genuinely legible, and genuinely **gates nothing**. The capability ladder calls E9 *persistent tiles, long-horizon stewardship*, and **nothing here persists**: the published `scheduled_relocation` rule says so in its own words — a work caught in the column "is lifted, carried to the sweep end point and set down there ALIVE; it is offline while airborne and **loses no hp**", with `damages: false` and **`gatesSecure: false`**. There is no tile that remembers, no state that accumulates across waves, and no E9 verb; the era is answered entirely with epoch-1 grammar. But the sweeps are emphatically *not* decoration, and my run is the loudest measurement of that I can offer: **20 sweeps started, 0 relocations, and `refusals.anchored` = 1,050.** The column reached my works one thousand and fifty times and the anchor hold refused it every single time. `relocations: 0` is a *choice* — all 24 works sit inside `anchor-center`'s r8 hold — not an absence, and `refusals.anchored` is the counter that proves the hazard was live while nothing appeared to happen. The reasoning it demanded was closed-form and available from the view alone: the claim is at (0,12); the only build ground within a turret's 16 of it is `center-anchor-bay` (x −10..10, z −8..8); the `center-devil-sweep` runs along z = 0 with `columnRadius` 4, cutting that bay in half; and the hold is the r8 disc inscribed in the bay. So the contract reduces to *place inside the disc*, which costs nothing and which I could compute before writing an order. What the run's difficulty actually was is somewhere else entirely: a continuous trickle of 927 kills' worth of thief-drones which, with **no stockpile standing**, all fall through to ordinary hero pursuit — `goldStolen` finished at **0** and `threats.alive` peaked at 27. The fields that carried it were `now.devilsAlley` (routes, `columnRadius`, `anchors[].holdRadius`, `sweepsStarted`, `relocations`, **`refusals.anchored`**), `now.works.entries`/`byKind`, `now.seams[].active/x/z/anchorIndex` (only two live, at (14,12) and (−14,−12), pinned all run; an inactive seam publishes all three as `null`), `now.gold` against `now.score.goldPanned`/`goldStolen`, `now.hero.hp/maxHp/x/z`, `now.threats.alive/wreckers/thieves`, and `now.orders[].status/reason`. Orders: `BUILD`, `HARVEST`, `PICK_UPGRADE`, `BLAST_AT`, `MOVE_HERO`, `REPAIR_UNDER` (never fired — nothing was ever wrecked), and one silence at the boundary. **My notebook remembers this map from generation 30, and it still plays the way I remember** — same claim, same three anchors at r8, same three crosswind routes, same four harvest anchors at (±14, ±12), same 2.4-second trickle, same w3 idle floor to the tenth of a second. The map is **not** named as cured this week, and its first minute confirmed it: two live seams funded a 50-gold turret at t ≈ 30 and nothing threatening happened until wave 2. What *did* move is the grammar, and here it moved **against** me: generation 30 rode a welded hero and never had to ask whether (0,0) was walkable. It is not.
report.winnability: Secured, and the margin was **wide for fifteen waves and genuinely thin at the close**: not one of 24 works was ever wrecked and the hero held its full running maximum through wave 10, but it bled to **46.2/175 (26.4 %) at t = 585.9** before a `field_dressing` pick took it back to 99.2 — roughly one more wave on that slope would have been a coin flip, while the *reel* margin (422 ticks, 3.5 % of the byte ceiling) and the *gold* margin (the cap itself) had nothing left to win.
report.lessons:
- **`MOVE_HERO` to a stake marker answers `UNREACHABLE_TERRAIN`, and my post order never advanced off it.** I planned the whole ride around walking the hero to `anchor-center` (0,0) so the fort would ring the body it defends; that point is a stake and refuses the hero, so the order failed in **all 91 views** and the hero never left (0,12). My own gen-79 rule says to emit `MOVE_HERO` once and **advance the post index only on an actual `UNREACHABLE` record** — I wrote the "emit once, drop when parked" half and not the "advance on refusal" half, so a one-line omission silently deleted the heat's main new lever. **A standing post needs a refusal-driven index; carrying the rule's first clause without its second is carrying none of it.**
- **Half my fort was therefore decoration, and it still secured — which prices the margin exactly.** With the hero stuck at (0,12), only 2 of 6 beacons (radius 8: (4,6) and (−4,6) at 7.2; the four at (±5,±5) at 8.6 and 17.7) and 3 of 4 turrets (range 16: (0,−7) at 19) could reach it. Compute the coverage circle against **where the body actually ended up**, not where you ordered it to go — and re-read `now.hero.x/z` every view to notice the difference. The fix for the next rider is free: bias the disc's works north (z ≥ 2) and probe a post at (0,5)-ish with a refusal-advanced ladder.
- **`refusals.anchored` is how you prove a hazard was live when its success looks like nothing happening.** 20 sweeps, 0 relocations, **1,050** anchor-holds. Gen 30 got 373 with 8 works; 24 works scale it linearly. When a mechanic's win condition is "nothing moved", find the counter that increments when it *nearly* moves — otherwise you cannot distinguish a load-bearing placement from a mechanic that never fired.
- **A thief-only roster settles the cap question by itself, and this is the third heat running I have carried the rule instead of re-deriving it.** `thief: true` forces `wrecker = false`, which deletes `REPAIR_UNDER`, palisade *bait* and every decoy idea (0 of 24 wrecked) — and it makes `stockpile` a trap, because a standing till is what makes `nearestGoldHolding` non-empty. Gen 106 overrode that warning with an estimate off a *concurrency* cap and lost 435 gold; I priced it properly this time and it is negative even bought LATE: at ~1.8 g/s of panning against the ~1.5–2 g/s a 4-thief rotation removes, 80 seconds of exposure earns ~84 against a 120-gold spend. **Declined, `goldStolen: 0`, 200 banked = the ceiling.** The "buy the pair late" refinement I have owed the notebook for three generations is now *priced and closed* on a map like this: it only pays where the till's trip time is long relative to the run's remainder.
- **Palisades on a no-wrecker board are still chewable, so they are a time sink and not a wall.** Non-wreckers gnaw blockers even though wreckers do not, so 14 palisades at 10 g flat were the right unbounded surplus sink (they absorbed and redirected, and none was lost) — but do not price them as permanent.
- **The plating-first scorer's SECOND tier earned its place for the first time.** Scoring `/heal|regen|mend/` at 80, just under plating's 100, took `field_dressing` at t ≈ 586 and turned 46.2/175 into 99.2/175 in the run's last fourteen seconds. On a board whose only loss is `hero_down` and whose pressure compounds to the final wave, the heal tier is not a tie-breaker — it is the endgame.
- **A hard build floor plus a bank gate landed the cap without ever starving the fort.** Always spend while the core is incomplete or `hp/maxHp < 0.75`; otherwise only when `(gold − cost) + rate × (600 − t) ≥ 205`, with `rate` read off `score.goldPanned` and **biased 10 % low on purpose** so the error direction is protective; and **no BUILD at all after t = 500**. Panned 1,010, spent 810, banked exactly 200 — and a flat floor cannot be argued with the way an `urgent` bypass can (gens 85, 101).
- **Silence at the boundary did its four jobs again, twenty-first contract running:** it took the `bank` default (`defaultedSecure: 1`), it kept the last accepted order 422 ticks inside a terminal tick this contract's `clockTicks` puts exactly at the secure instant, it held a 93-view run to 91 entries, and — the reason that matters most — **it cannot be rejected**, so the replay cannot diverge the way gen 84's nearly did.
- **Ride the skeleton first and change nothing — twenty-second heat where that is the whole discipline, and the sixteenth in a row where it secured on ride one.** Two runs total. The reading budget went to the era pins as a per-contract diff, the roster flags, the loss reason, the published relocation rule and the buildables roster; the riding budget went to the unmodified generation-6→111 skeleton (ONE ladder with ONE ordinal per id priced at its live instance off `buildables[].costs[standing]`; a rung with no candidates left RETIRED rather than stalling the rungs behind it; a refusal blacklist partitioned into GROUND — poison the coordinate — and ECONOMY — retry, poison nothing; `Number.isFinite` seam filtering before any sort; blocks of six alternating across the live seams; `BLAST_AT` above the traveller; a blank line at `pendingSecure`). 24 builds, zero ladder stalls.
- **An era named for rebuilt maps can leave a map's rules untouched, and proving it is a result — tenth heat running.** Grep the pins for the contract id first, confirm the twist and geometry against the notebook, then one ten-second idle probe against the remembered floor. Four minutes, and it redirected the whole budget from geometry to the one thing the board does differently.
